quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What should you know about the oily strip down the center of a lane?

options.text: Only ride on it if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
It usually gives good grip, unless it is raining.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually gives good grip, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip of the road is usually oily but gives enough grip for safe riding, unless it rains. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide. Riders can ride on either side of the strip and still be in the center of their lane.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars to get the best grip.

questions.question: How can you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will make you sober. Your body needs time to remove the alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose so it can flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and be comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snug enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Why shouldn't a motorcyclist rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can be dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: You must use more than just mirrors to stay aware of your surroundings. Motorcycles have blind spots like all other vehicles.

questions.question: What are the best colors for motorcycle riders to wear?
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green colors help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machines, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply steady pressure to both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation should riders use?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while giving each rider enough space. Use single file only when turning, entering highways, or exiting highways.

questions.question: When it rains, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
On the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: What should you wear to protect your hearing while riding?

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent this damage.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Always turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change. Leaving it on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: When you ride beside another vehicle, you may be in its blind spot and the driver cannot see you. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your ability to ride safely?
questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: How should your arms be positioned when holding the handlebars?

options.text: Bent with a large bend at the elbow.

questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: During a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, both the rider and motorcycle lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, the motorcycle leans while the rider stays more upright.

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful and provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
It brakes automatically by learning your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes when the rear brake pedal is applied. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.
